entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5714"/><title type="x-s2">PSALM 25</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Ps.25.1-Ps.25.22">Psa 25:1-22</reference>. The general tone of this Psalm is that of prayer for help from enemies. Distress, however, exciting a sense of sin, humble confession, supplication for pardon, preservation from sin, and divine guidance, are prominent topics.</title> <div sID="gen8698" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5714"/><hi type="bold">1. lift up my soul--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Ps.24.4">Psa 24:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.86.4">86:4</reference>), set my affections (compare <reference osisRef="Col.3.2">Col 3:2</reference>). <div eID="gen8698" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: PSALM 25 Psa 25:1-22 . The general tone of this Psalm is that of prayer for help from enemies. Distress, however, exciting a sense of sin, humble confession, supplication for pardon, preservation from sin, and divine guidance, are prominent topics. 1. lift up my soul-- ( Psa 24:4 ; 86:4 ), set my affections (compare Col 3:2 ).

His trust in God is fixed.<div eID="gen8714" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8715" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">net--</hi>is frequently used as a figure for dangers by enemies (<reference osisRef="Ps.9.15">Psa 9:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.10.9">10:9</reference>). <div eID="gen8715" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5727"/><div sID="gen8716" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5727"/>16-19. A series of earnest appeals for aid because God had seemed to desert him (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.13.1">Psa 13:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.17.13">17:13</reference>, &c.), his sins oppressed him, his enemies had enlarged his troubles and were multiplied, increasing in hate and violence (<reference osisRef="Ps.9.8">Psa 9:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.18.48">18:48</reference>). <div eID="gen8716" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 16-19. A series of earnest appeals for aid because God had seemed to desert him (compare Psa 13:1 ; 17:13 , &c.), his sins oppressed him, his enemies had enlarged his troubles and were multiplied, increasing in hate and violence ( Psa 9:8 ; 18:48 ).

In conscious innocence of the faults charged by his enemies, he confidently commits his cause to God. Some refer--</hi> <div eID="gen8719" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8720" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">integrity, &c.--</hi>to God, meaning His covenant faithfulness. This sense, though good, is an unusual application of the terms. <div eID="gen8720" type="x-p"/>
